I'm a 60-year-old farmer in Quzhou, been working this land for 40 years since my father handed it to me. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension pamphlets and do the basic math, but honestly I trust what I've seen with my own eyes more than what some young technician tells me in a classroom. My wife and I farm 15 mu — 10 mu in wheat-maize double crop and 5 mu in cotton. Our son works at a factory in Handan and sends money home, but he can only get back for the big harvests, so labor is tight. We have a tube well, which is a blessing, but electricity for pumping gets more expensive every year.

**Wheat (10 mu):** I plant in mid-October, around the 12th to 15th, once the autumn rain has softened the soil. I'm using Jimai 22 this year — Old Wang down the road got 500 kg/mu with it last year, and my saved seed from the previous variety was looking a bit weak. I'll buy about half the seed, save the rest. Before planting, I'll spread about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu (15-15-15) and plow it in. That's my base. Then at jointing in late March, I'll topdress with 15 kg of urea per mu. The extension fellow says 12-14 kg N is enough, but two years ago when I cut back to 12 kg, my wheat went yellow and I only got 420 kg/mu. Last year I used about 15 kg N total and got 480 kg/mu. So I'm sticking with 15 kg N per mu — better to waste a little fertilizer than lose a quarter of my yield. I'll irrigate three times: once after planting if it's dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling in May. Three times is what we've always done. I'll spray herbicide once in early spring, and if I see powdery mildew, I'll spray fungicide.

**Maize (10 mu):** This is planted right after wheat harvest, usually June 12th to 15th. The window is brutally tight — sometimes only five or six days. I used to till between wheat and maize, but now I mostly no-till plant directly into the stubble with my neighbor's planter. Saves time and the stubble keeps some moisture. I'm using Zhengdan 958 hybrid — it's 50 yuan per mu for seed, which hurts, but the yield is reliable. At planting I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, then at the big trumpet stage (around late July), I topdress with 12 kg urea per mu. Total N about 13-14 kg/mu. If July is hot and dry, I'll irrigate once at trumpet stage and maybe once at filling in August. But if we get good summer rains, I might only irrigate once or not at all. Maize can take some drought better than wheat. One round of herbicide at planting, that's usually enough.

**Cotton (5 mu):** I plant in late April. This year I'm growing Xinluzao on the southern 5 mu — that land is a bit sandier and cotton likes it. I plow in March and put base fertilizer: 40 kg compound fertilizer per mu. Then urea at budding (early July, about 8 kg/mu) and again at flowering (late July, another 8 kg/mu). Total N around 12 kg/mu. Cotton needs water at flowering and boll filling, so I'll irrigate twice — mid-July and mid-August. But cotton also needs more pesticide. I spray herbicide before planting, then insecticide 3-4 times for bollworm and aphids. That's expensive, maybe 300-400 yuan for chemicals alone on these 5 mu. Picking is the hard part — my wife and I do most of it by hand in September and October. If the price looks good, I might hire two local women for a week to help pick, but that costs 150-200 yuan per day each, so I only do it if I'm confident the price will stay above 7 yuan/kg.

**Why I'm doing it this way:** Last year was decent — wheat gave me 480 kg/mu, maize about 500 kg/mu, cotton 260 kg/mu of seed cotton. I'm not changing much. My son says I should try less fertilizer to save money, but he's not the one who has to look at yellow wheat in April and worry about whether we can feed ourselves. I have about 6,000 yuan cash set aside for inputs this year. The fertilizer and seed will take most of it, but I'll have enough. I always leave a buffer — what if the pump breaks? What if my wife needs medicine? I'll spend about 8,500 yuan on the whole year, maybe a bit more if I hire pickers. I expect about 450 kg/mu wheat, 500 kg/mu maize, and 250 kg/mu seed cotton. Not trying to break records — just trying to make sure we don't have a bad year.
